title: rustls ClientConfig + reqwest blocking; end-to-end authenticated GET
description: Build a rustls ClientConfig with a ClientCertResolver returning the cert chain + custom signer. Hand it to reqwest::blocking via preconfigured TLS. Perform an authenticated GET. This is the spike payoff.
acceptance_criteria: spike bin gets HTTP 200 from the local SoftHSM-backed mTLS test server using the token-held key.
close_reason: core::client builds rustls ClientConfig (aws_lc_rs provider, default protocol versions incl TLS1.3) with the token-backed resolver + reqwest::blocking. Spike --url does mTLS GET. PROVEN: HTTP 200 (TLSv1.3, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384) from the SoftHSM-backed mTLS server using the token-held RSA key. Note: open_identity login made optional (Some(pin) for SoftHSM; None for CSPid cached agent).

title: Port rustls-pkcs11 signer onto open_identity (client-auth SigningKey)
description: REFINED APPROACH: do NOT vendor rustls-pkcs11 wholesale (it duplicates session/discovery, which 7um's core::pkcs11::open_identity already does WITH label selection it lacks). Instead reuse open_identity and port only the signer (~150 LOC) from rustls-pkcs11 (MIT, attribute in comment): a rustls SigningKey/Signer that maps SignatureScheme->cryptoki Mechanism, calls Session::sign (C_Sign), and converts ECDSA r||s -> ASN.1 DER. Wrap in a ResolvesClientCert returning a CertifiedKey built from Identity{cert_der,private_key,session}. Port the FULL mechanism map (EC + RSA-PKCS1 + RSA-PSS) so we're key-type-agnostic before we know the real token. Build+test against SoftHSM (EC now; optionally add an RSA identity to exercise the PSS path offline).
design: RESEARCH RESULT: existing crate rustls-pkcs11 (github.com/mdelete/rustls-pkcs11, MIT, v0.1.1 2026-06, ~410 LOC, cryptoki 0.12 + rustls>=0.22) already implements the rustls ResolvesClientCert + SigningKey + Signer bridge to cryptoki. Source (not README) confirms it advertises RSA-PSS (needed for TLS1.3), RSA-PKCS1, ECDSA P256/384/521, EdDSA; maps SignatureScheme->cryptoki Mechanism, converts EC r||s to ASN.1, session in Arc<Mutex>, logs in with PIN at resolver construction. CONCLUSION: do NOT hand-roll the signer. Adopt/vendor this crate. KEY GAP: cert/key discovery is 'first found' (ObjectClass::CERTIFICATE + KeyType, no label/ID selection). If the CSPID token holds multiple certs (auth/sign/encrypt), this will pick the wrong one -> must fork to add label/ID filtering. Maturity risk: 0 stars, unproven -> prefer vendoring the 410 LOC so we control it and learn from it.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/integration test: signer signs test data with the SoftHSM key; signature verifies against the cert public key. EC P-256 path proven now; RSA-PSS path proven if an RSA SoftHSM identity is added. (Real-token mechanism confirmed under lx7.)
notes: CONFIRMED via cspid_selftest at work: key=RSA, RSA-PSS available, TLS 1.3, and signing works on the AGENT-CACHED login (no explicit C_Login). => Build signer for RSA-PSS ONLY (RSA_PSS_SHA256/384/512 -> Mechanism::Sha*RsaPkcsPss). Drop EC signing (YAGNI; EC cert stays as label-selection decoy). NO PIN handling in app: open session, do NOT call login (add only if a sign returns CKR_USER_NOT_LOGGED_IN).
close_reason: Signer built (core::signer): Pkcs11SigningKey/Pkcs11Signer map rustls RSA_PSS_SHA256/384/512 -> cryptoki Mechanism::Sha*RsaPkcsPss, C_Sign on token; Pkcs11ClientCertResolver presents CertifiedKey from open_identity. RSA-PSS-only (EC dropped, YAGNI). PROVEN in-container: SoftHSM RSA auth-cert, TLS 1.3 handshake to openssl s_server returns HTTP 200 -> server validated our on-token RSA-PSS signature. Ported from rustls-pkcs11 (MIT, attributed).

title: Spike: investigate ISC CSPID PKCS#11 capabilities
description: Research Information Security Corporation (ISC) CSPID: what it is, its PKCS#11 module (path/name), supported key types (RSA/EC) and mechanisms (esp. RSA-PSS), PIN/login model, and platform support. Aim to pre-answer the 'Confirm at the office' checklist where docs allow, and inform uov (signer) + lx7 (real module).
design:
FINDINGS (ISC CSPid, infoseccorp.com):
PRODUCT: software 'virtual smartcard' exposing a standard PKCS#11 API. Keys stored in AES-256 password-protected PKCS#15 files on local/network drive. FIPS 140-3 L1 (CMVP #4998; 2019 sheet said 140-2/PKCS#11 v2.20, site now says v3.20). Our rustls+cryptoki+C_Sign approach is CORRECT and unaffected.
MODULE: libcspid.so on UNIX (cspid.dll on Windows); default install /opt/cspid. Confirm exact path (e.g. /opt/cspid/lib/libcspid.so) at office.
ALGOS: RSA up to 8192-bit AND ECDSA up to 571-bit; hashes SHA-256/384/512. Both key types possible -> real credential's type still TBD at office.
LOGIN/PIN: password cached by the CSPid SYSTEM-TRAY AGENT. On UNIX only PER-SESSION caching (cache dies when agent exits; agent must be RUNNING). Explains the browser 'just working'. Confirm whether our app passes a PIN or relies on the agent cache, and that the agent runs in the target env.
DAS MODE: in DAS/role-based config, libcspid.so DELEGATES C_Sign (and C_Decrypt key-unwrap) to a remote DAS server. Transparent to our code (still Session::sign) but adds network latency and means key may be server-side. 
REGISTRATION: apps calling C_Initialize are tracked in a 'registered applications list' (register via cspid_ui --register on Windows). Likely our app must be registered/authorized to use the token in a locked-down env. Confirm enforcement + Linux registration method at office.
STILL OFFICE-ONLY (not in public docs): RSA-PSS mechanism support (pkcs11-tool -M) -> decides TLS1.3 vs forced TLS1.2; actual key type; exact module path; registration enforcement; agent/PIN flow.
notes: Informs uov + lx7. Findings to be recorded here and in PLAN.md.
close_reason: Spike complete; findings recorded on bead + PLAN.md. Approach validated (libcspid.so, standard PKCS#11). Remaining unknowns (RSA-PSS, key type, path, registration, agent/PIN) require the real module at the office.

acceptance_criteria: spike bin prints the cert subject and confirms a usable private-key handle against the SoftHSM token.

Spike verified in-container vs SoftHSM: auth-cert->CN=auth-cert, sign-cert->CN=sign-cert (distinct certs => label selection discriminates), missing label errors cleanly. cryptoki 0.12 API notes for uov: CInitializeArgs::new(CInitializeFlags::OS_LOCKING_OK); AuthPin::new(Box<str>) i.e. pin.into(); Session::find_objects does full init/find/final; get_attributes(h,&[AttributeType::Value])->Attribute::Value(der).

title: Hardening + point at real CSPID module
description: PIN handling (cached/env/prompt), error messages for common failures (wrong label, locked token, handshake failure), swap to the real CSPID .so and key label, verify against a real internal API.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated request succeeds against a real internal API via the real CSPID module.
notes: Login/PIN model largely RESOLVED: CSPid agent auto-starts per session + caches password -> token available with no manual PIN (same path as Firefox). User confirmed cert objects readable via a Python pkcs11 module with agent running. App registration not a hard gate (Python reached the token). REMAINING PROOF: a private-key C_Sign with no manual PIN (cert-read != sign; sign needs logged-in session). Design: try opening session WITHOUT C_Login first; only add login if signing fails. PIN-handling work likely minimal/none.

title: Share PKCS#11 context across requests (concurrency + latency)
description: Each requests_pkcs11.request() call does Pkcs11::new + C_Initialize and drops to C_Finalize. Reviewer finding on l39: with the GIL released, two Python threads calling request() concurrently share the module's global state — thread B's C_Initialize can fail with CKR_CRYPTOKI_ALREADY_INITIALIZED, or thread A's drop-time C_Finalize can invalidate thread B's live session mid-handshake. Also heavyweight per-call (dlopen + initialize), which may matter for real CSPid latency. Fix: process-wide Once/shared context, or a session-reusing client class.
acceptance_criteria: Two Python threads calling request() concurrently both succeed against the test server; repeated sequential calls reuse the initialized context.
